courses.title: Quantum I
courses.subtitle: Probability, amplitudes and wave mechanics
prerequisites: Mathematical toolkit, Classical mechanics, Electricity & magnetism and Waves. Calculus, complex numbers, ODEs, Fourier transforms, inner products and eigenvectors are used; each lesson links local preparation. Numerical shooting and spherical/radial coordinates are bridged locally.
coverage: Three dimensions and orbital angular momentum
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory single-particle nonrelativistic wave-mechanics course, not all quantum physics or a full university/laboratory credential.

courses.title: Quantum II
courses.subtitle: States, operators and composite systems
prerequisites: Quantum I and Mathematical toolkit: complex vectors, matrix products/eigenvectors, inner products, probability and calculus. Every lesson links prior local preparation; trace/partial trace, spin half-angles, coherent-state series and rotating-frame terms are taught explicitly before use.
coverage: Coupling, detuning and driven two-state models
States when outcomes or partners are unobserved
General angular momentum and orbital rotations
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory abstract-state/spin/composite course, not exhaustive quantum mastery or a university/laboratory credential.

courses.title: Quantum III
courses.subtitle: Approximation, transitions and scattering
prerequisites: Quantum II and the Mathematical toolkit. Explicit local bridges cover approximation order, Airy/delta/gauge/solid angle, continuum rates, Green/Legendre functions and Kraus maps before use. Each lesson links its precise prior preparation.
coverage: A bounded introduction to open systems
Choose, test and report an approximation
courses.scopeNote: A defined introductory approximation/transition/scattering course with explicitly bounded atomic and open-system examples, not all quantum methods or a university/laboratory credential.

courses.title: Advanced analytical mechanics
courses.subtitle: Predict how things move using energy. Start with a bead on a wire, then work up to swinging pendulums, spinning objects and orbits.
coverage: Follow moving constraints and their forces
Find orbit shapes and test their stability
Describe rotation of a rigid body
Read nonlinear motion and the onset of chaos
Change canonical variables and use Hamilton–Jacobi
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected ideal models and short calculations, with deeper reasoning you can open. Longer problem-solving practice and specialized topics lie outside this focused first course.
beyondScope: Nonholonomic constraints such as general rolling without slipping need a separate treatment.
Detailed rigid-top motion, Euler-angle conventions and general orbit quadratures are beyond this first pass.
Chaos is introduced through concepts and diagnostic limits; there is no new numerical chaos simulator in this course.
Action-angle variables, perturbation theory and advanced Hamilton–Jacobi boundary problems are further study.

courses.title: Fluid dynamics
courses.subtitle: Follow a drop of water. Find out how liquids and gases move through pipes, slide past walls and carry momentum.
coverage: Follow a moving piece of fluid
Describe flow near walls and through pipes
Use forces to predict fluid motion
Compare flow scales, wall effects and turbulence
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected flow models and short calculations, with definitions and deeper notes you can open. Longer derivations, numerical flow simulation and specialized topics lie outside this focused first course.
beyondScope: Potential-flow solutions, circulation and lift need further treatment.
Surface waves, surface tension, rotating flows, stratification and instability theory are further study.
Compressible gas dynamics, shocks, heat transfer and non-Newtonian fluids need additional equations and models.
Turbulence is introduced through scales, fluctuations and averaged momentum transport; this course does not provide a turbulence solver or numerical flow simulator.

courses.title: Plasma physics
courses.subtitle: Follow charged particles in a gas. Study how they shield a charge, circle in a magnetic field and carry waves.
coverage: Follow orbits, drifts and magnetic reflection
Build a simple plasma fluid model
Compare plasma waves and small disturbances
Connect particle distributions to fluid quantities
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Detailed sheath solutions, Coulomb collision operators and transport coefficients need further study.
Full magnetized wave spectra, kinetic dispersion integrals and quantitative instability thresholds are outside this first course.
Magnetic confinement design, reconnection, turbulence, strongly coupled and quantum plasmas require more advanced models.

courses.title: General relativity
courses.subtitle: Use rulers, clocks and falling objects to explore how gravity changes the geometry of space and time.
coverage: Connect geometry to energy and momentum
Use black-hole, wave and expanding-universe models
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Detailed tensor derivations, rotating black holes and causal diagrams.
Numerical relativity, strong-field waveforms and observational cosmological inference.
Quantum fields in curved spacetime and quantum gravity.

courses.title: Advanced experimental methods
courses.subtitle: Use repeated readings to test a prediction. Learn how to correct a measuring tool, estimate uncertainty and report what you found.
coverage: Turn a question into a measurable comparison
Separate scatter, bias and shared uncertainty
Fit a model and inspect its misses
Make the procedure and result repeatable
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Specialist instrument design, laboratory safety procedures and equipment-specific training.
Advanced experimental design, nonlinear inverse problems and full Bayesian inference.
Detailed uncertainty budgets for a particular real experiment.

courses.title: Quantum information
courses.subtitle: Start with a qubit, a quantum system with two basic measurement outcomes. Study how to change it, measure it and share information across several qubits.
coverage: Describe a qubit and its measurement
Describe noise as a change of state
Protect a qubit and use interference in small algorithms
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Full fault-tolerant architectures, quantum cryptography and communication protocols.
Large algorithms, complexity proofs and hardware performance claims.
Continuous-variable systems and complete quantum process tomography.

courses.title: Advanced many-body physics
courses.subtitle: Track groups of particles by counting how many occupy each state. Explore what changes when the particles influence each other.
coverage: Add, remove and count identical particles
Use an average field and test its limits
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Detailed Green-function calculations, diagram expansions and numerical many-body methods.
Superconductivity, topological phases, strongly correlated materials and real material modeling.
Full phase diagrams and quantum critical dynamics beyond the stated toy models.

courses.title: Quantum field theory
courses.subtitle: Start with a field value at each place. Follow its wave patterns to see how quantum theory counts particles and predicts interactions.
coverage: From a field to quantum modes
Build the action for a simple field
Create, remove and count free particles
Control short-distance sums and state the theory’s limits
courses.scopeNote: These modules teach selected models and short calculations, with optional definitions and deeper reasoning. Longer derivations, research methods and specialist topics need further study.
beyondScope: Spinor and gauge fields, quantum electrodynamics and the Standard Model.
Full loop integrals, renormalization proofs, nonperturbative methods and curved spacetime.
Research-level scattering calculations and experimental particle-physics analysis.
